verdict_reason: The index pin is real (name plus exact key order) but stops at declaration - no explain plan proves the planner uses it - and the test violates the repo's @BeforeEach cleanup rule by leaking an all-null Address into the shared collection.

todos.issue: The test asserts only that the index is DECLARED (name + key order from listIndexes); it never runs an explain plan, so it cannot detect the failure it claims to guard - a declared index the planner does not actually choose for findByOrganisationIdAndStatus or the searchBy* $or/regex queries (COLLSCAN or in-memory SORT) still passes green.
todos.fix: Add a behavioural assertion alongside the metadata one: run an explain (e.g. mongoTemplate.execute(db -> db.runCommand(new Document("explain", findCommand))) or Query with a real page+sort) for findByOrganisationIdAndStatus and assert winningPlan reaches an IXSCAN on indexName 'org_status_created' with no SORT stage.

todos.issue: Cleanup is inline at the top of the test body instead of @BeforeEach, and the test then saves an all-null Address (builder().build(), no organisationId/status) that is never removed - it leaks into the shared 'addresses' collection of the shared Spring context/Mongo container for whatever IT class runs next; every sibling IT (AddressGetIT, AddressSearchIT, OperatorListIT etc.) only survives this because each happens to call deleteAll() in its own @BeforeEach.
todos.fix: Move the deleteAll() into a @BeforeEach setUp() per the repo convention, and drop the save() entirely - auto-index-creation:true already creates the collection and index at context startup, so no document is needed to observe listIndexes.

todos.issue: assertThat(indexNames).doesNotContain("crn_status_type_created", "org_status") is vacuous: neither name appears anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms only this line), the Mongo container is created fresh per run, and Spring's auto-index-creation only creates indexes declared on @Document classes - so no mechanism can ever put those names in the list and the assertion cannot fail. It reads as a migration guard against a stale deployed index, which a throwaway container structurally cannot see.
todos.fix: Replace it with an exhaustive assertion that actually bites - assertThat(indexNames).containsExactlyInAnyOrder("_id_", "org_status_created") - which catches index bloat, renames and accidental extra @Indexed fields.

todos.issue: The pin covers key names and key order but not sort directions: extracting(IndexField::getKey).containsExactly(...) passes unchanged if createdAt flips from -1 to 1 (or organisationId/status flip to -1), even though the class javadoc and Address.java both make 'newest-first' load-bearing. Flipping the whole def to descending would silently break Pageable sorts that the equality-prefix reverse scan cannot rescue.
todos.fix: Extract the pair, e.g. .extracting(IndexField::getKey, IndexField::getDirection).containsExactly(tuple("organisationId", ASC), tuple("status", ASC), tuple("createdAt", DESC)), so the assertion matches the @CompoundIndex def exactly.

todos.issue: The test omits the mandatory // Given // When // Then comment blocks that every other IT in this repo carries, and mongoTemplate.indexOps("addresses") hardcodes the collection name instead of deriving it from the entity, so a change to @Document(collection=...) on Address is not caught by the type system.
todos.fix: Add the // Given // When // Then blocks per the repo IT convention, and use mongoTemplate.indexOps(Address.class) so the collection name is resolved from the @Document annotation.
